name: Data.conjHolWeight_kernelWeight_bounds
summary: The size bound from the bound for lowest K-types of a parameter with gap; dominance and gaps by the sign of each index and the sums of column lengths.

steps.claim: Not a step of the proof: lines 78–80 are the rest of the statement, which ends before the `:=` on line 80 (a second-reader message). The line census takes the `:=` of `let s :=` on line 78 for the start of the value, so the check requires these lines to be owned here. They state: with s = signsW(D, j) and k = conjHolWeight(j, τ): |k(i)| ≤ 5·b(D) for every i; k and kernelWeight(j, τ) are K-dominant for s and orderW(j); both have holomorphic gap 300·nStar(D) for s.
steps.lean:
lemma conjHolWeight_kernelWeight_bounds τ : let s := D.signsW j; let k := conjHolWeight j τ; (∀ i,
      |↑(k i)| ≤ 5 * D.b) ∧ IsKDominant s (orderW j) k ∧ IsKDominant s (orderW j) (kernelWeight j
      τ) ∧ HasHolGap s k (300 * nStar D) ∧ HasHolGap s (kernelWeight j τ) (300 * nStar D) := by

steps.claim: Split into the five assertions and introduce the indices.
The size bound: |lowestKType| ≤ the bound for parameters with gap (`abs_lowestKType_le`, `Data.hasGap_paramW`, w(m + 1, τ) ≤ 2b).
steps.lean:
grw [← Int.cast_abs, abs_lowestKType_le (D.hasGap_paramW _ τ).neg (L := 2 * D.w (D.m + 1) τ)
    (by grind [Pi.neg_apply, paramW]), card_rowIndex]; simp; grind [nStar_bounds, w_le_two_mul_b]

steps.claim: Dominance: by the sign of each index, from the definition of orderW and monotonicity.
steps.lean:
iterate 2 cases Int.units_eq_one_or (D.signsW j ‹_›) <;> simp_all
    [orderW, -tsub_le_iff_right] <;> gcongr

steps.claim: Gaps: each column length colsMinus(τ, ·) is at most their sum, which is bounded through nStar (`Data.nStar_bounds`).
steps.lean:
all_goals simp [*, -Nat.cast_sum]; grw [← Finset.single_le_sum (f := (untwistedAuxPair
    j).colsMinus τ) (a := D.m - j)] <;> grind [-Sum, Int.ofNat_le.2 D.nStar_bounds.2.1]
